narrative.title: Express Lane or Back of the Queue
narrative.scenario: A print spooler processes a stream of jobs, and every job arrives with a priority flag: flag 1 joins the back of the queue, flag 0 cuts straight to the front. The spool is a linked list, so front insertion rewires one pointer while back insertion must walk to the tail first. After the whole stream is processed, the spool order is reported.
narrative.inputFormat: A sequence of pairs (value, indicator) where indicator 1 appends value to the end of the list and indicator 0 prepends it to the front; the list starts empty.
narrative.outputFormat: The contents of the linked list after every operation, read front to back.

testCases.explanation: Each flag-0 job jumps the queue, so the two front insertions end up in reverse arrival order ahead of the appended jobs.
All flags are 1, so arrival order and final order coincide.

hintLevels: Level 1: Two insertion flavors — front insertion makes the new node the head; back insertion finds the tail and hangs the node after it.
Level 2: Front insertion is O(1): point the new node at the current head and return it. Back insertion walks to the last node whose next is null.

Level 3: The subtle bug is order-dependent flags — front insertions applied later end up earlier in the list, which is exactly what the sample's 5,2 prefix shows; also guard the empty-list case for back insertion.
